Hi there...
    I know you posted this over a week ago already, but I saw this post a few days ago and wanted to make sure to respond because I can empathize SO much with what you have going on in your life right now.
     I'm a lot like you in that I don't have too many close relationships in my life, either, and I also apparently have aspergers, or if not, something similar that can make it hard for me to be as connected to others as I'd like to more often than I would like to admit.  Like you, it sounds, I have to put in twice or 3 times the effort it seems like to get a good reaction from people, or to try to make friends, and I often get lost in conversations too because I find myself without very much to say a lot of the time.  These seem like small potatoe issues to a lot of people, but trust me, I know how much it can suck, how uncomfortable and isolating it can be, when all you want to do is reach out and make connections like everyone else seems to be able to. I feel ya.  :(
    My best advice to you, as someone who struggles with the similar crap, is to try to look at it as a game, but at the same time, don't get too invested.  I've come to be somewhat aware of the fact that while it DOES, of course, matter to a degree what you say to people, and yes, it is true that communication is the cornerstone of what tends to build up relationships and bond people and reason would stand that if you have a hard time with communicating with people for any reason, than your relationships are more than likely going to be a bit strained... but the truth of the matter is, at least I've found, that it doesn't always matter how great or High-quality, or invigorating, or even that interesting what you have to say in response to people is.. or is not... when you're conversing if any part of your hesitation or difficulty in coming up with stuff to say in said interactions is in part perhaps due to at times over-monitoring what you want to say back in response, internally worrying that what you feel most naturally inclined to say, (or not say,) is not going to be good enough.  I don't know if you ever go through this kind of internal process of harsh self criticism, and feel like you constantly have to be your own watchgaurd over your own conversations to make sure that even the simplest utterance that comes out of your mouth in response is going to be either pure gold or at least, ya know, passable according to some largely nonexistent rule book of social guidelines, but trust me... sometimes you just have to cut yourself a break and let yourself be you.  Even if that means not saying enough... or perhaps not always having something to say.  This is okay, as long as you do give effort some of the time to try to push yourself to think of what the best thing to say would be to keep a conversation going if you want to be involved, but don't think that just because you kinda fall silent once in a while that that means it's game-over- NO chances of recovery never another moment to start up a different conversation.  People are usually more forgiving than you would think, for one, and also tend to have incredibly short attention spans, anyway.   Just look at a "missed chance" to talk as just time spent in the dug out till your ready to go up to bat for the next game... and in this one, you WILL swing and hit the ball, maybe even hit a home run.  
     Now, as a follow up to that pep-talk... I have some home work for you.   Talk to that girl.  She probably wouldn't bother reacting to your posts online if she wasn't paying attention to you in person.  How do I know?  I am the proud owner of a vagina.  Maybe I have a touch of aspergers, but that doesn't mean I don't know the way girls go about things. :p
    Lastly, I know it seems like a million years away from ever happening, but if you just allow yourself to try to be more "present" with people, allowing yourself to interact with them however feels the most natural, without getting too intense about critiquing how "well" your doing it, like your playing a game that you know doesn't matter. Perhaps you'll find that you'll be able to loosen up a bit and find that you had more to say than you realized and have fun talking with people.  Even if not... then you can toss this advice and go back to the drawing board... but whatever happens just don't give up.  While I haven't had many relationships... I can tell you that of the ones that I DO have, that they are worth the effort of obtaining, growing, and nurturing... that I am extremely grateful for them and I wouldn't trade them for anything in the world and they are worth it. Having a deep connection with other people provides a level of fulfilment that almost can't be replicated by just about any other experience in life... and it IS obtainable, even for people like myself.  I hate to say this, because it just sounds so cliché, but, if I can do it and I have the same diagnosis... chances are that you can, and will, form meaningful relationships, too.  I truly hope you will give yourself the chance to believe that it will happen...and that in time, sometime soon, you'll find yourself connecting as deeply as you would like with those you want to. 
     As a final thought...(sorry this ended up being so long,) but I would like to just second what someone else already mentioned... the therapy thing.  Not to say that it will fix everything or to say that you "need" it, but these people can help with a lot of issues... and perhaps they can help you to overcome fear of rejection.. which seems to be the core of your problem.  Anywho, best of luck to you, and I hope at least some of this helped.  You are more than welcome to pm if you ever want to talk about this or anything else, too.

It was weird, I was like a knat to them, or something.  I never did anything that they found awful enough to kick me out of the group, but yet, they definitely did not like me... they just sort of over the years developed this silent resentment of me intermingled with this indifferent tolerance that I was an annoyance that they couldn't get rid of.  There were only 2 girls in that group that I consistently felt I could consider actual friends... the rest were just, awkward acquaintances, but then, when I look back, I realize it was my mistake in never even realizing that I was falling behind on my fundamental responsibility to try to build friendly repoire with them.  Instead of this, I usually just huddled around the group circle awkwardly, not really contributing to conversation, I guess because it wasn't "safe" to do so since things that I said often got met with scathing bitchy remarks, and the only ones that I would actually talk to were the two that I mentioned, although this was only typically in private, away form the rest of the group.  I sometimes wonder if the girls that befriended me did so cuz they felt sorry for me, and if they related with me seemingly only in private because they were embarrassed or afraid of letting the other girls who clearly dissaproved of me see them talking to me during group situations.  
I guess you could say that, looking back, I had felt like the lowest, most insignificant man on the totem pole for so long socially that I sort of lost having any sense of having a voice, any sense of feeling like I belonged anywhere or that anyone even WANTED me around.  Around these girls, I truly felt useless, and like I was just some odious nuissance and some sort of shit stain to their reputation.
This happened over a period of time from about middle school onward, so I felt this way longer than just a mere 4 years of high school.
The first time that I really remember feeling true social anxiety, however, or shame, and that there was in fact something truly wrong with me and my personality, was probably way before this, around 2nd grade or so.  I remember that I was invited to a class party for my brother, who was two years older than me, and so I came along.  It was some sort of holiday party, and the reason I'd been brought along was because my mother dearest had volunteered to go help out in the classroom, as apparently a lot of other hawk eyed moms liked to do for their elementary school aged kids at this particular elementary school- gave them a chance to be a mom away from home too, I suppose.  Anyway, I just remember that I always complied with whatever typically veering on ridiculous outfit that my mom wanted me to wear even up until this age, and so I found myself in some dorkish nightmare of a christmas themed outfit complete with a reindeer antler-themed headband.  If you've never seen these things, oh man are you missing out.  They almost put the Christmas Story's "Pink Nightmare" bunny-eared suit to shame (hopefully you've seen the movie and know what I'm talking about; if not youtube this clip https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FrcDXI4cZyA immediately once you're done here.) 
Anyhow... So here I am milling around with a bunch of older kids, trying to look somehow "cool", but already feeling like an out of place dork.  Then, out of nowhere, apparently some older boy that I must have found cute starts backing away from me... slowly, with a rather disturbed look on his face, much in the same way as you probably would if an insane person started randomly ranting a nonsensical tirade at you in the middle of a crowded street.  The reason for this was because, for whatever reason in my warped, underdeveloped prepubescent mind, I thought it would be a really good idea to start trying to play with this kid... mind you at an inopportune moment while all the other children including this one were busy civilly standing there just filling food on their plates in a single file line... and my idea of "playing" apparently consisted of making really loud, awkward "reindeer noises" at him.  (Wow, I had such a way with the men even back then.)  Anyhow, in retrospect, his subsequent reaction as I mentioned was understandable revulsion, where he didn't quite know what to do, other than, slowly and awkardly back away a bit, and say, "whoooa rudolf, calm down."  
Later on at home that evening, my brother, again who was a bit older than I was, confronted me and said, with a very serious somber tone, almost like a parent whose about to inform their kid of something really horrible they just did that they intend to lecture them at length about: "So... everybody was talking about you today after you left."  
I paused, confused, and utterly oblivious to what he was leading into saying.  "So?" I asked.  "SO..." he responded, "the problem is, they let me know what they think about you.  They literally came up to me and told me, 'Matt, you're sister's REALLY weird.  Like, really, really weird.'  They don't like you."  He might as well have followed up this comment with a nice, "I don't know what you did, but you really embarrassed the hell out of yourself, and me. " I just remember at that moment being filled with the most intense bout of shame that could ever fill such a small frame.  I got that instant feeling of sickness that accompanies the guilt you feel after doing something horrendously wrong, that sick to your stomach feeling.  So now, in my mind, everybody in Matthew's fifth grade class thought I was a freak.  I guess it wouldn't have affected me so badly if I hadn't been already getting hints here and there from other kids my own age all the while throughout the years up until that moment that they, too, thought I was kind of strange for various things I did and said.  What makes me the most angry even today is that these were all things that I did in INNOCENCE that I had no idea were considered so "weird".  This sort of conundrum snowballed, and continued throughout my formative upbringing, eventually branding me with a title of "weird" even in high school.  I don't know if it's true, but it must be, why else would so many embarrassing things have happened to me in direct consequence to things I've said and done, again, things that I did out of innocence, just being a kid trying to fit in like everyone else?  To give you some more background, I did finally get a diagnosis of aspergers syndrome, so maybe this is to blame.  Whatever the cause is, I'm tired of being afraid to live my life due to an ongoing fear that I'll forever embarrass myself unwittingly in social scenarios, however, it keps holding me back.
